habek--haemosu.scene: INTRODUCING HABEK, god of the Amnok River, who keeps his borders the way kings do, and his daughters the same way. Late afternoon on the Amnok, moments after the sun god went up in a flash of copper: Habek stands on a wet black boulder in mid-current as if the river were his throne hall, mist curling round his robe hem like a dais. Worm's-eye angle from just above the water: he leans forward from the waist, hands clasped behind his back, long white beard swinging forward, glaring DOWN past the lens at his daughter in the shallows: "Who stopped the chariot. Say a name." Jowly face set hard, brows knotted, mouth a thin flat line — a magistrate, not a father. Behind him, painted in drifting white mist: cold teal water (#2f8f7a), dark pines on the far bank dissolving into haze, and a copper-gold streak still fading in the clouds. The low copper sun breaks through the mist and rakes across his face, beard and pale blue robe; teal light bounces up off the river. At the bottom frame edge, out of focus: the bowed head and pale ice-blue silk shoulders of his daughter in the water.

geumwa--haemosu.scene: INTRODUCING KING GEUMWA, the gold-frog king of Buyeo — found under a rock, raised in a palace, kind to strays. Late afternoon in the Buyeo palace yard: the iron-studded timber doors have just swung open and the king has come out to the yard himself. Low three-quarter angle over the shoulder of a barefoot, dust-grey exile woman kneeling on the packed earth (only her out-of-focus shoulder and dull ice-blue hanbok sleeve at the frame edge): he is mid-step down off the last stone step, one fist gathering his heavy red-burgundy robe, the other hand half-raised, palm up, beckoning her to stand. A warm, dry, crinkle-eyed half-smile, head tilted: "Come in. I've got a room free." Behind him, painted loosely in warm dusty haze: the opened studded doors, a palisade of sharpened timber teeth, grey roofs climbing a hill, drifting dust motes as bokeh. A low sun-shaft through the gate rakes across his face, gold crown and gold embroidery; khaki-gold (#a89a72) lives in the dust haze, the robe stays red-burgundy.

jumong-exile--buyeo.scene: INTRODUCING JUMONG, the best archer in Buyeo — barely grown, about eighteen, and the princes have noticed. Morning in the princes' archery square: packed earth, a weathered timber mark-stake out of frame. Low worm's-eye three-quarter angle from beside his front foot: he is at full draw with a long wooden bow, the string at the corner of his grinning mouth, one eye half-closed down the arrow shaft, red headband tails lifting in the breeze, and he says, easy and cocky: "I'll take the fly." A boyish lopsided grin, eyes bright with mischief; completely clean-shaven, no moustache, no beard. Behind him, painted in soft morning haze: grey palace roofs, a timber palisade, dust drifting across the square, and two princes in blue and green Buyeo robes as dark out-of-focus shapes at the far edge, arms folded. The low morning sun rakes across his face, the taut bowstring and his red silk from the side in warm red-orange light (#e8563f), deep painted shadow on the far side.

daeso--buyeo.scene: INTRODUCING DAESO, Buyeo's crown prince — good with a bow, until someone is better. The princes' mark-stake in the Buyeo practice square, late afternoon; the foundling's arrow has just landed dead centre. Low three-quarter angle: Daeso, a grown young man, stands too close to the camera, his own bow gripped hard and low at his side, a sheathed ring-pommel sword at his hip, half-turned and leaning in toward someone just off-frame, jaw tight. A cold, controlled face: brows low, eyes narrowed and flat, nostrils tight, the corner of his mouth pulled down, saying quietly: "Do not outshoot the house that feeds you." Behind him, painted in amber dust haze: the weathered timber mark-stake with one arrow still quivering in it, grey palace roofs, a palisade, and a red-robed archer as a dark out-of-focus shape at the frame edge. The low afternoon sun rakes across him from the side in hard khaki-gold light (#9b8f6a), half his face falling into deep painted shadow.

galsa--buyeo.scene: INTRODUCING GALSA, Geumwa's younger son — he smiles at everything, for now. The same afternoon at the princes' mark-stake, one beat after the foundling's arrow lands and his older brother goes cold. Over-the-shoulder angle past his brother's dark blue sleeve (out of focus at the frame edge): Galsa stands a step back, hands raised mid-clap and frozen an inch apart, a bright polite smile on his face that never reaches his eyes, which slide sideways toward his brother and then down to the dirt: "If it lands, I meant to applaud." A sheathed ring-pommel sword at his hip. Behind him, painted in warm dust haze: packed earth, the timber mark-stake with a quivering arrow, grey Buyeo roofs and a palisade melting into a pale gold afternoon sky. The low side sun rakes across his face and green silk; moss-green (#6b8f4a) lives in the shadows and the leaf-dappled haze.

ladyye--buyeo.scene: INTRODUCING LADY YE, Jumong's young wife in Buyeo — a girl with a steady hand and a long memory. Night in their room in the Buyeo palace, moments after an assassin's knife went through the quilt: the knife still stands upright in the bedding behind her. Low three-quarter angle from the floor: she kneels upright beside her small oil lamp, one hand cupped round its flame to keep it alive, turning her head to look straight at her husband off-frame, braids swinging. Her face is pale but completely steady — level dark eyes, lips pressed, no tears — as she says: "Leave Buyeo. Tonight. I'll keep the lamp." She wears exactly the sheet's dress: a BLUE hanbok with mustard-ochre sleeves, a red-and-gold embroidered collar and a red sash, braids and gold hairpin — not pink, not a rose robe. Behind her, painted in warm smoky darkness: timber walls, a paper-lattice window with blue night beyond, a door left half open onto a dark corridor, lamp smoke curling. The little lamp lights her face and blue silk from below in warm amber; a faint rose warmth (#d98fa8) lives only in the lamp smoke and on her cheek, the room falling off into deep painted umber shadow with floating dust specks as soft bokeh.

haewonmek--buyeo.scene: INTRODUCING HAEWONMEK, a fetch of the underworld — black hat, black silk, and a mouth bound shut so he can't haggle. Night rain over a river below Buyeo with no ford and no boat: he skims low over the black water toward the lens, coming to collect the day's dead, his robes and hat tassel streaming behind him. Low three-quarter angle from the wet stones of the bank: he leans forward into the flight like a hawk, one sleeve swept back, a long straight ring-pommel sword in a black scabbard held low along his side. Under the wide black brim his lean young face is mostly in shadow; a strip of black silk binds his mouth shut, and only his eyes catch the light — patient, cold, a clerk come to collect. Behind him, painted in slanting silver rain and river mist: dark pines on the far ridge, the river churning grey-violet (#6b5b6e), a crow on a bare branch. A white-violet lightning flash from the side rakes across his hat brim, eyes and wet silk; raindrops as soft bokeh.

yeontabal--jolbon.scene: INTRODUCING YEON TABAL, chief of Jolbon — he shows thieves his storeroom on purpose. Dusk in the Jolbon valley: his scouts have just dragged a stranger in red silk across the packed-earth yard, and Tabal stands on the edge of his grain porch holding a cup he is not drinking. Low worm's-eye angle from the yard: he leans one heavy forearm on a porch post, tiger pelt over his shoulders, the untouched cup hanging from his fingers, and looks DOWN at the stranger (only a red-silk shoulder, out of focus at the frame edge) with hot, narrowed, measuring eyes, beard jutting, mouth a hard line: "So who sent you." Behind him, painted in dusk haze and cookfire smoke: grey giwa roofs of five clans that will not share a yard, a great crooked pine, the well, a ridge with the last orange light, the first torches lit as warm bokeh. A torch on the porch post rakes across his face, beard and pelt from the side in hot amber-brown (#a97c4a), the far side falling into deep painted shadow.

sosuno-widow--jolbon.scene: INTRODUCING SOSUNO, Tabal's widowed daughter — she has priced every man in the yard, and she has not finished with this one. Late afternoon on the grain porch at the Jolbon hunt muster: she is running the valley before anyone has asked her to. Low three-quarter angle from the yard: she stands on the porch edge with one foot up on a millet sack, a bow in her fist, jabbing an arrow like a pointer at a hunter off-frame, head half-turned, already looking past him to the next man: "West line. Two short. You. Spear. Not that one, the one that isn't bent." Sharp brows, cool appraising eyes, mouth mid-command, utterly unimpressed. Behind her, painted in warm dust haze: a rack of leaning spears, grey giwa roofs, a great pine, hunters as soft out-of-focus shapes in plain Jolbon hemp. The low sun lays a dusty-gold stamp (#e8a04a) across the porch boards and raking light across her face; her robe stays dusty rose, never gold.

jumong-king--jolbon.scene: INTRODUCING KING JUMONG, the first king of a valley that still smells of millet. Night in Tabal's torchlit hall: the five tribes have just done the thing they hate more than a ditch — they agreed — and voted him king. The moment of the crown: he kneels on one knee on the packed-earth floor while two weathered hands in a tiger-pelt sleeve (only the hands and sleeve, at the top frame edge) settle the gold flame crown onto his head. Low three-quarter angle: he tips his face up into the crown with a crooked, half-disbelieving grin and steady warm eyes, answering: "I will. Not for the chair. For the roof." Now that he is king, the short moustache and goatee of the sheet are allowed. Behind him, painted in drifting torch smoke: timber posts, stacked millet sacks, the five clans' animal banners as soft dark shapes, torches as warm bokeh. A torch at his side rakes across his face, the gold crown and the red dragon robe in hot red-orange (#e8563f); deep painted shadow on the far side.

sosuno-queen--jolbon.scene: INTRODUCING QUEEN SOSUNO, the first queen of a country that still smells of millet. Her first morning as queen, in the Jolbon granary: the cord on the millet sacks is still new, and the sacks have not learned to be tribute. The moment of the crown: she sits sideways on a stack of corded millet sacks in her new crimson-and-gold queen's robe, one knee drawn up, pushing the last jewelled pin into her braided crown with one hand, a wooden tally stick in the other. Low three-quarter angle: she glances sideways at the sacks with a cool, appraising half-smile, counting already — a merchant who has just been handed the whole storeroom. Behind her, painted in drifting millet dust: rough plank walls, timber posts, sacks stacked into the dark. Low morning sun-shafts through the gaps in the plank wall rake across her face, hair ornaments and gold embroidery; the dust motes glow dusty-gold (#e8a04a) as bokeh, the robe stays crimson.

bidam-elder--gi.scene: INTRODUCING BIDAM, fifty-one, the new first chair of the Harmony Council — every vote now passes through his hands. A winter afternoon in the council chamber in Seorabeol: old Supum's seat has just been given to the one councillor who never told the queen what she wanted to hear. Low three-quarter angle across the end of the long council table: he settles back into the first chair, one elbow on the armrest, a string of 108 dark prayer beads rolling slowly through his fingers, head tilted, watching the ring of councillors (dark out-of-focus shapes in Silla court robes and black feather caps) with a faint self-amused smile and flat, unhurried eyes — the man who is about to say "I object." Grey at the temples, slicked-back hair, clean-shaven; his long white outer robe has galloping horses embroidered on the sleeves, over a plum-magenta inner robe. Behind him, painted in drifting incense smoke: timber pillars, paper doors glowing blue with snow-light. A bronze brazier at his side lights him from below in warm amber; deep navy (#141C2E) fills the room's shadows and glints on the beads.

sukwon--gi.scene: INTRODUCING SON SUKWON, about fifty, Bidam's father — a man of few words who has saved them all for his son. Before dawn at the gate of the Hwarang yard, his son's first morning: the packed earth is still dark. Over-the-shoulder angle past the back of a sixteen-year-old boy's head and white hwarang shoulder (out of focus in the foreground): Sukwon stands close, both hands raised behind the boy's head, tying the boy's headband once, tight, and looks down at him with grave, quiet, searching eyes, mouth barely moving: "Bidam… Do you know the meaning of your name." Grey hair swept back, clean-shaven, the sheet's black outer robe over a brown inner robe with a white collar — a plain True Bone father, not a courtier. Behind him, painted in blue pre-dawn mist: the timber yard gate with its tiled roof, a thin band of first light over the ridge, the yard's packed earth fading into haze. A paper lantern hanging on the gate post lights his face from the side in warm amber; slate-blue (#3d4654) fills the dawn shadows.

jinduk-princess--gi.scene: INTRODUCING PRINCESS SEUNGMAN, forty-five, the queen's cousin and the last of the Sacred Bone — kind, careful, and never once surprising. A grey winter afternoon at the palace gate in Seorabeol: word of the council vote has reached her before Bidam has. Over-the-shoulder angle past a tall man's out-of-focus white silk sleeve at the frame edge: she has hurried out to catch him, the hem of her coral-pink robe gathered in one fist, her other hand half-raised toward him, leaning in, face open with dismay — brows lifted, eyes wide and hurt, lips parted: "Bidam…! What is this I hear? Surely not…" A gentle woman of forty-five, long black hair under her gold floral hair crown. Behind her, painted in cold winter haze: the red pillars and snow-dusted tiled roof of the palace gate, a pale grey-violet sky, a pair of lanterns as soft bokeh. A low winter sun breaks through the gate and rakes across her face and gold embroidery; violet (#9d7bd0) lives in the cold shadows and the haze.

kotoku--gi.scene: INTRODUCING KING KŌTOKU, the King of the East — his politeness comes with a price list. No character sheet: he is a refined Yamato man of about fifty, a long narrow face, heavy-lidded courteous eyes, a thin moustache and a small neat chin beard, wearing the 7th-century Asuka-period Yamato court dress: a small black lacquered gauze cap with a short stiff tail, a round-collared robe of deep purple silk over white, a black belt, a flat pale shaku tablet in his hands — NOT a samurai, NOT Heian or Edo robes, NOT a Chinese emperor. Afternoon in his audience hall at Naniwa: unpainted cypress pillars, a raised wooden floor, bamboo blinds half-rolled over a white gravel courtyard and the bright sea beyond. Low three-quarter angle: he leans forward on a low armrest on his dais, head tilted in polite apology, a gracious smile that does not reach his measuring eyes: "With respect — I must refuse peace with the Divine Country." At the frame edge, out of focus: the back of a kneeling Silla envoy in a magenta court robe and black feather cap. Sun through the bamboo blind stripes his face; a pale rose cast (#e89ab0) through a silk curtain.

yumjong--gi.scene: INTRODUCING YUMJONG, a quiet True Bone who drinks his tea slowly and listens fast. A winter evening in Bidam's tea room in Seorabeol: Bidam recruits with tea and long silences, and Yumjong is the first man to drink the tea. Low three-quarter angle across the low tea table: he holds a celadon tea bowl in both hands just below his lips, not drinking yet, his eyes sliding sideways over the rim toward his host with a mild, sly, unremarkable half-smile: "The islands, now. Last summer it was the emperor's war. Your Lord Chunchu does get around." Long grey hair, grey moustache and goatee, the sheet's white robe with a crimson collar and sash. At the frame edge, out of focus: Bidam's white sleeve and a hand with prayer beads. Behind him, painted in drifting kettle steam and incense smoke: a paper door glowing blue with snow-light, a timber post, a hanging scroll gone to shadow. A small charcoal brazier under the iron kettle lights him from below in warm amber; violet (#8a68c9) lives in the steam and the shadows.

ibiga--suro.scene: INTRODUCING IBIGA, the sky god — cloud is his body, and he does not usually look down. HIGH IN THE OPEN SKY above the mountains of the south, late golden afternoon: he drifts on his own cloud, his robe and lower body trailing off into billowing white cloud, and for the first time in a thousand flights he stops. Low three-quarter angle from just below the cloud bank: he leans out over the cloud's edge on one forearm, the other hand pushing back his wild black hair, staring DOWN past the camera at a jade-green ridge far below — arrested, lips parted, brows drawn up, eyes caught and unable to look away: "That ridge… That woman." The background is a VAST BRIGHT SKY, not black: towering sunlit cumulus painted in loose cream, gold and deep blue strokes, wind-torn wisps, and far below through a gap a misty jade mountain ridge whose skyline curves like a reclining woman. The low gold sun rakes across his face, bare chest and the folds of his blue robe; deep sky blue (#1e4d9c) fills the cloud shadows.

jeonggyeon--suro.scene: INTRODUCING THE LADY OF THE RIGHT VIEW, goddess of the mountain — the ridge was a woman before anyone noticed. On the summit of her ridge, late afternoon: mist streams across jade-green stone and pine, and above her the sky has just begun to come down, a vast blue cloud lowering onto the ridge. Worm's-eye angle from the ridge path: she sits enthroned on a moss-covered jade outcrop as if the mountain were her country, her red chima spilling down over the rock until silk and stone are hard to tell apart, hands folded in her white sleeves. She does NOT look up; she looks straight ahead along her ridge, chin level, regal and unhurried, the corner of her mouth curling in a cool knowing challenge: "Why has heaven come down. To look? Or… to touch." Behind her, painted in streaming mist: pines, ridge after ridge fading blue, falling leaves, the descending blue cloud filling the top of the sky. The low sun breaks through the cloud and rakes across her face, jewelled hair crown and silk; lavender (#c084fc) lives in the mist.

suro--suro.scene: INTRODUCING KING SURO, born from a golden egg, and in no hurry to marry anyone local. Dawn on Guji hill above the Gaya coast: a golden egg has just split open on a bed of red silk at the summit, and he rises out of it already grown and already dressed, as myths allow. Low three-quarter angle from the grass beside the shell: he kneels up from the broken gold eggshell halves, one hand resting on the shell's jagged rim, the other brushing shell-dust from his purple sleeve, and looks out over the land below with a calm, curious, faintly amused look — unbothered, self-possessed, a king who has not yet been told he is one. Small gold crown on his topknot, black headband, light stubble, the sheet's purple robe with gold trim. Behind him, painted in dawn haze: other unbroken golden eggs half-hidden in the grass, the misty Gimhae plain, the river mouth and the sea, the torches of the singers on the slope below as warm bokeh. The rising sun rakes across his face, the gold shell and the purple silk in warm gold (#e0a33c), deep painted shadow on the far side.

heohwangok--suro.scene: INTRODUCING HEO HWANG-OK, the princess from far across the sea — she sailed farther than anyone in Samhan had heard of, and arrived dressed for it. Sunset off the Gaya coast: her red-sailed ship is just coming in to the beach of Golden Gaya. Low three-quarter angle from the deck: she stands at the prow rail, one hand on the carved rail, wind pulling at her braid and silk, looking toward the shore with a confident, amused, appraising half-smile and slightly narrowed eyes, as if she has already decided what she thinks of the king waiting there. Twenty-one, warm brown skin, blue-black braided hair with gold ornaments, the sheet's purple jeogori with patterned sleeves and violet chima. Behind her, painted in sea spray and evening haze: the great red sail filling half the frame, the wake, the Gaya hills and beach in soft haze, gulls, the first lamps on the shore as bokeh. The low sun rakes across her face and silk from the side; rose (#d98fa8) glows through the red sail and the sunset haze.

muryuk--muryuk.scene: INTRODUCING MURYUK, the youngest son in the surrender cart — Gaya handed over its crown; it did not hand over him. A BOY of about fifteen: the sheet's face made young — smooth-cheeked, NO beard, NO moustache, long black hair tied back — and NO armour and NO sword: a plain dark travelling robe with a purple cape. Late afternoon on the slow road from Geumgwan toward Silla: the cart creaks along the riverbank and his two older brothers sit facing front. Low three-quarter angle from the roadside: he kneels up in the back of the ox-cart, twisted round, both hands gripping the cart's wooden rail, looking back over his shoulder at the harbour he is leaving — jaw set, eyes wet but stubborn, memorising it: "Somebody should remember what it looked like." Behind him, painted in golden river haze: the river bending away, the Gaya harbour with tiny ships and the smoke of iron forges shrinking into the distance, his brothers' backs and Silla spearmen as dark out-of-focus shapes. The low sun breaks through cloud behind the harbour and rakes across his face; purple (#8B5CF6) lives in his cape and the river haze.

jinduk-queen--queen-jinduk.scene: INTRODUCING QUEEN JINDUK, the last polite miracle of the Sacred Bone. Coronation morning in the great hall of the palace in Seorabeol, the censers still warm after the rebellion: the crown was made for her cousin and has to be padded at the temples. The moment of the crown: she sits perfectly, rigidly still on the throne while a goldsmith's hands (only his hands and plain Silla artisan sleeves, out of focus at the frame edge) tuck folded silk under the gold tree-and-antler crown at her temple, because someone told her once that the old queen never fidgeted. Low three-quarter angle from below the dais: chin level, shoulders squared, holding her breath, her gentle eyes sliding sideways with solemn, anxious resolve, lips just parted: "Yushin… preserve the sacred country…" Long black hair, the sheet's red robe with gold horses and phoenixes and blue shoulder panels. Behind her, painted in drifting incense smoke: red pillars, bronze censers, banners, kneeling officials as dark shapes. A shaft of pale winter morning light through the open hall doors rakes across her face and the gold and jade of the crown; violet (#9d7bd0) lives in the incense haze.

inmun--huangdi.scene: INTRODUCING KIM INMUN, nineteen, Chunchu's second son — he reads Tang characters better than his father would like. No character sheet: a slim young Silla nobleman, handsome clever narrow face, fine straight brows, quick dark eyes, clean-shaven, hair in a topknot under a small black Silla gauze cap with two upright pheasant feathers, a sky-blue silk Silla robe with a white collar and a dark sash, plain silk sleeves, no armour, no bracers. Afternoon in a Chang'an ward office, the day the Silla embassy is registered: the clerk counts them as a number, not as names. Over-the-shoulder angle past a Tang clerk in a green round-collared robe and black futou cap (out of focus at the frame edge): Inmun leans over the clerk's shoulder, one hand flat on the desk, eyes cast DOWN at the register, which lies just below the bottom frame edge and is never seen — no book, no paper, no writing anywhere in the picture — his brows drawing together, a quick troubled intelligence in his eyes as he understands before his father does: "…Father?" Behind him, painted in sunlit dust: a lattice window, the rammed-earth wall and grey-tiled gatehouse of the ward, a busy Tang street as soft shapes. A shaft of afternoon sun through the lattice rakes across his face; pale sky-blue (#6fb0d8) lives in the cool shadows.

gaozong-prince--huangdi.scene: INTRODUCING LI ZHI, twenty, crown prince of Tang — heir to everything, and the first man in Chang'an to laugh. Late afternoon on the imperial polo ground: he and the foreign prince have played until the dust has made them the same colour. Low three-quarter angle from the ground beside his horse: he sits a dusty bay horse and twists round in the saddle, laughing with his whole shoulders, a long polo stick with a crescent head resting over one shoulder, sweat and dust on his face, eyes crinkled with plain happiness at the rider off-frame: "When I am emperor — No. That sounds like a curse." The sheet's face and his cream-white silk robe with gold dragon embroidery, sleeves bound up for riding, the hem dusty. At the frame edge, out of focus: another rider's magenta Silla sleeve. Behind him, painted in golden dust haze: the long rammed-earth wall of the ground, vermilion-pillared pavilions with black-grey tiled roofs and green-glazed ridges, Tang banners, the dust cloud of the game. The low sun rakes across his face and the horse's neck from the side; tan-gold (#b8935a) glows in the dust.

wuzetian-consort--huangdi.scene: INTRODUCING WU, twenty-four, a lady of the inner palace — the screen is doing very little of the hiding. Night at the farewell banquet in the Tang palace: she is supposed to be behind the tall painted silk screen at the side of the hall, and she is working the whole room from there. Low three-quarter angle from the hall floor: she leans out past the edge of the screen, one hand resting on its lacquered frame, her face and one shoulder in the light, the rest of her still behind the painted silk, gazing out over the banquet with a slow, knowing, red-lipped half-smile and heavy-lidded eyes that miss nothing — a glance that steadies a maid and slows a minister's cup. The sheet's face, high black hair with gold ornaments and long gold tassels, the red robe. Behind her, painted like a Chinese historical drama in incense haze: vermilion pillars, two facing rows of banquet tables and seated officials as soft dark shapes, red lanterns and many small flames as warm bokeh, cool blue-green shadow beyond. A bronze lamp-tree beside the screen rakes warm gold light across her face; pink (#e879a6) lives in the silk sheen and the haze.

taizong--huangdi.scene: INTRODUCING LI SHIMIN, the Second Emperor of Tang — nobody in Chang'an writes his name, and he has just said it to a foreigner, on purpose. Late night in his private hall, the last game of go: the board is out, the stones half-played, the room hushed. Low angle from the level of the go board, the camera below his eyeline: he sits behind the board, broad and heavy and still, one big hand resting on the lid of his stone bowl, leaning slightly forward into the lamplight, looking across at his guest (only an out-of-focus magenta Silla sleeve at the frame edge) with heavy, tired, searching eyes and the faintest predator's ease at the corner of his beard: "Is it correct now?" The sheet's face: black futou cap with the upright pin, thick black beard, the imperial yellow robe-cape over black brocade. Behind him, a Tang palace at night like a Chinese historical drama: lattice doors backlit in cool blue-green, a painted screen, incense haze, a red lantern far back, a dark reflective floor; his shadow huge on the wall. A single oil lamp beside the board rakes up across his face and the heavy yellow folds in warm amber (#c97a2e), falling off into black across half his face and body.
